World Development Sustainability, 2, [...] In sum, future flooding is certain (Rizwan et al. 2023, Ali et al. 2021, Mehmood et al. 2021). The problem lies not in the hazards themselves, but in the failure to anticipate, adapt, and protect. sources.title: Understanding vulnerability to flood-induced disasters: a comprehensive scoping review on at-risk individuals and evacuation challenges
sources.excerpt: Roma communities in Romania found that recurring floods destroyed makeshift homes, left residents without shelter, spoiled food supplies, and rendered clothing unusable . [...] The collected evidence highlighted overlapping vulnerabilities among multiple groups during flood-induced disasters. Figure 4 provides a visual synthesis of these intersections, showing that certain groups–such as individuals with low income, those in inadequate housing, persons with disabilities or chronic conditions, the elderly, and socially isolated individuals–were frequently reported in the literature as intersecting with multiple other vulnerability factors. By contrast, categories such [...] strategies. Building on the insights of recent reviews, it contributes to bridging the gap between theoretical advancements and real-world implementation. Given the complexity and fragmented state of existing evidence, a scoping review is the most suitable approach to map the literature, clarify definitions, and identify knowledge gaps. This review aims to explore how vulnerability is defined, addressed, and operationalized in the context of flood-induced disaster evacuations in HICs.
